Thanks — attaching capacity_estimate_v3.xlsx (summary below). Draft runbook notes and recommendations:

Summary assumptions (from BrightMart doc + call): baseline ~20 qps steady, peak 250 qps typical, worst-case 1,000 qps Black Friday spike; avg tokens/request ~80. Target user-facing p95 200ms.

Option A — Conservative baseline (higher committed)
- Baseline: 12 x A10G-equivalent GPUs (model quantized FP16/INT8 path)
- Expected steady throughput: ~220 qps with p95 < 200ms (with batching and KV caching)
- Autoscale: min=12 GPUs, max=20 GPUs; scale step=2 GPUs; cooldown=60s
- Burst: small hot pool (2 warm nodes) + rapid cold spin-up beyond hot pool (expected cold start ~35–60s)
- Use for customers needing minimal latency variance.

Option B — Elastic baseline + larger burst pool (recommended for cost/balance)
- Baseline: 8 x A10G-equivalent GPUs
- Expected steady throughput: ~140 qps; covers normal days with margin
- Autoscale: min=8, max=32 GPUs; scale step=4 GPUs; cooldown=45s
- Warm pool: 4 warm standby GPUs (kept with warmed KV and warmed JIT kernels) — these serve first-minute burst traffic with p95 ~220ms
- Cold spin-up beyond warm pool: ~45s median; plan for synthetic warming immediately before marketing windows via a scheduled keepalive traffic job

Option C — Minimal baseline + aggressive burst (for cost-sensitive customers)
- Baseline: 4 GPUs; min=4, max=40; big burst pool with 6 warm nodes + elastic cold spin-up. Accepts higher risk of slightly higher p95 during initial burst.

Technical considerations / mitigations
- KV cache warmup: keep warm pool nodes pinned with periodic requests to maintain KV cache validity for top 10% of prefixes. This reduces cold-penalty on first requests.
- Continuous batching: tune batch windows by endpoint; for chat-style short requests prefer small micro-batches to keep latency low.
- Quantization: recommend INT8 for customer model to increase tokens/sec and reduce memory pressure (saves ~30% GPU memory).
- Canary & pre-production test: run a 48-hour canary at 1.2x expected peak with synthetic traffic; schedule a 2-hour promo warmup before major marketing sends.
- Cost modeling: see spreadsheet; rough estimate for Option B baseline + 4 warm nodes + 2-hour per-week promo burst to 32 GPUs = $X/hr baseline + $Y/hr burst (numbers in capacity_estimate_v3.xlsx).

Operational runbook items (short)
- Pre-promo checklist: schedule warmup job, validate KV caches, check quota mappings for region, inform on-call SRE.
- Fallback: if autoscale cannot provision GPUs due to capacity, route to cheaper fallback model (smaller model variant) for degraded latency but functional responses; include UX messaging to customers if required by BrightMart.
- Post-event debrief: capture perf metrics, adjust warm pool sizes based on observed p95 and token burn.

Next steps / action items
- Lauren: confirm which option BrightMart prefers (A/B/C) and any procurement constraints.
- Marissa: prepare cost/commercial language for the contract: baseline commit, burst overage rate, and a 1st-year burst discount option to discuss with Marcus.
- Marcus: confirm commercial room for discount and SLA language.

I'll attach the Excel with per-node throughput tables and cost projection. Ping me if you want me to join procurement call with BrightMart.
